original_question: Is the set of all Eisenbud-Neumann diagrams of the boundary divisors D arising from minimal smooth SNC-completions of contractible surfaces, or of acyclic surfaces, or of Q-acyclic surfaces, of log-general type finite?
target_in_paper: Zaidenberg’s Question 1.6 on p. 16, later restated by Zaidenberg as the “Finiteness Conjecture [Za2]”: for a smooth Q-acyclic surface X of log-general type, with minimal smooth SNC-completion (V,D), is the set of possible Eisenbud–Neumann diagrams of D finite? ([ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp](https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/9311/ojm34_02_10.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right finiteness theme, the role of a minimal smooth SNC-completion and its boundary divisor D, the Eisenbud–Neumann/dual-graph-at-infinity viewpoint, and the log-general-type setting. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~orevkov/tono.pdf))
missing_details: The paper-faithful target is the Q-acyclic case; adding a separate disjunction over contractible, acyclic, and Q-acyclic surfaces broadens the problem beyond the standard restatement of Zaidenberg’s conjecture closest to your wording. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4c6be8c9a13a1bd4e0209d988cd19815c388797f&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The surface should be specified as a smooth complex affine algebraic surface X. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4c6be8c9a13a1bd4e0209d988cd19815c388797f&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
Q-acyclic should be spelled out as b_i(X)=0 for all i>0, i.e. X has the rational homology of a point. ([hse.ru](https://www.hse.ru/data/2023/10/12/2056626372/Summary.pdf))
Log-general type should be stated as logarithmic Kodaira dimension 2. ([hse.ru](https://www.hse.ru/data/2023/10/12/2056626372/Summary.pdf))

The completion data should be made explicit: (V,D) is a minimal smooth SNC-completion, with V smooth complete and D the reduced simple normal crossings boundary at infinity. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=4c6be8c9a13a1bd4e0209d988cd19815c388797f&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The minimality condition is implicit in your draft but should be stated: D contains no rational (-1)-component D_i with β(D_i)=D_i·(D−D_i)≤2. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~orevkov/tono.pdf))

Finiteness should be understood up to combinatorial type, i.e. up to isomorphism/homeomorphism of the resulting graph/diagram, not literally as a set of embedded divisors. ([hse.ru](https://www.hse.ru/data/2023/10/12/2056626372/Summary.pdf))

The object should be named precisely as the Eisenbud–Neumann diagram attached to D; nearby citations of the same question also phrase it as the topological type of the dual graph at infinity. ([ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp](https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/9311/ojm34_02_10.pdf))
refined_question: Over C, let X be a smooth Q-acyclic affine algebraic surface of log-general type, meaning that b_i(X)=0 for all i>0 and the logarithmic Kodaira dimension of X is 2. If (V,D) is a minimal smooth SNC-completion of X — i.e. V is a smooth complete surface, D is the reduced simple normal crossings boundary at infinity, and D contains no rational (-1)-component D_i with D_i·(D−D_i)≤2 — is the set of combinatorial types of Eisenbud–Neumann diagrams associated with D finite? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~orevkov/tono.pdf))
justification: I chose this formulation because your mention of Eisenbud–Neumann diagrams and Q-acyclic surfaces matches Zaidenberg’s later polished restatement of his 1995 question almost verbatim, while Orevkov’s citations identify the source as Question 1.6 on p. 16 of alg-geom/9506006. The later clarifying remarks also supply the hidden hypotheses needed to make the problem stand alone: smoothness, affineness, the Q-acyclic condition in Betti-number form, log Kodaira dimension 2, and the precise minimality condition on the SNC boundary. This keeps the question as close as possible to the paper’s intent while removing the over-broad contractible/acyclic disjunction in the draft. ([ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp](https://ir.library.osaka-u.ac.jp/repo/ouka/all/9311/ojm34_02_10.pdf))
